title: Origami handoff: ergonomic adapter for TypeScript async-iterator <-> Web Streams
creator: Miles Chen
description: Problem: teams keep encountering awkward edge-cases when converting between async-iterable generators and browser/worker ReadableStream/TransformStream in our TypeScript SDK. Current examples either swallow cancellation, lose backpressure semantics, or make retries (with partial consumption) unsafe. Goal: ship a small, documented adapter library ("Origami Handoff") that provides ergonomic, well-tested primitives for interop: asyncIterableToWebStream, webStreamToAsyncIterable, cancellableTee, and resume-friendly shims for retry semantics. The adapter should be small (single-file utility + tests), have clear migration examples for app authors, and be the canonical recommended approach in SDK docs and examples.
acceptance_criteria: API surface: asyncIterableToWebStream(source, opts) and webStreamToAsyncIterable(stream, opts) available in ts-sdk v3.4.0
Cancellation: cancellation on either side propagates to the underlying source and releases resources (e.g., abort signals forwarded, underlying iterator .return() called)
Backpressure: when consumer drains slower than producer, WebStream backpressure and async-iterator pull semantics are preserved (no uncontrolled buffering > configurable limit)
Idempotent retries: a documented pattern + helper that allows safe retry of requests that were not partially committed by user apps; helpers MUST surface when partial data was consumed
Tests: unit tests for normal flow, consumer-cancel, producer-throw, slow-consumer backpressure, and retry detection (5 tests each scenario)
design_notes: Design goal: keep adapter orthogonal to our runtime concerns (no direct runtime imports). It should only rely on standard TS types + minimal polyfills for Node/Deno where ReadableStream is missing

Key trade-offs considered: eager buffering vs strict backpressure. We choose a bounded queue approach with configurable highWaterMark and a drop/throw policy optional. Defaults aim for low memory with helpful debug messages.

Cancellation model: prefer explicit AbortSignal plumbing. When converting async-iterator -> WebStream, adapter will create an AbortController and expose it via opts so callers can cancel. For webStream -> asyncIterable, the iterator will call stream.cancel() when iterator.return() invoked.

Retry semantics: adapter will expose a small helper `captureFirstChunk(source)` that can detect if any bytes/tokens were emitted before a transient error; the SDK can use that to decide safe vs unsafe retry. We will not attempt automatic replay of arbitrary generators.

Ergonomic API shapes: provide both low-level primitives and a high-level convenience wrapper `dualStream(sourceOrStream)` that normalizes to an async iterator with metadata (origin, aborted, firstChunkSeen).
implementation_plan: 1) Create single file src/stream/origamiHandoff.ts with exported functions: asyncIterableToWebStream, webStreamToAsyncIterable, cancellableTee, captureFirstChunk, dualStream
2) Implement bounded queue using simple Promise-based push/pull pairs to ensure deterministic backpressure (no external queue deps)
3) Wire cancellation: pass AbortSignal into generator via opts.onCancel callback; ensure iterator.return() triggers sourceCleanup path
4) Add TypeScript types and JSDoc examples; include browser and Node test harness (use undici polyfill for ReadableStream in Node test runner where needed)
5) Add unit tests under test/stream/origamiHandoff.test.ts covering racey cancellation, slow consumer, and retry-detection logic
6) Documentation: update docs/sdk/streams.md and add migration snippet in examples/streams/origami-handoff.md
7) Create a small e2e example app in examples/chat/origami-demo that demonstrates streaming server response -> browser WebStream -> UI incremental rendering and controlled retry on network blip

8) Benchmarks: microbench for throughput and memory with producer emitting 1k tokens at varying consumer delays; target no more than 1.5x baseline memory compared to direct iterator consumption with default highWaterMark=8
testing_plan: Unit tests for each exported function and failure modes (mock async-iterators that throw on 2nd yield)
Integration test: Node harness that pipes an async generator to a TransformStream consumer that delays per-chunk and asserts no OOM and backpressure observed (measured by producer await points)
Browser test: Puppeteer script that mounts WebStream to ReadableStream -> shows bytes in DOM; simulate user cancel and verify underlying generator.return() called
Fuzz test: randomized chunk sizes & interleaved cancels to detect race conditions
Regression detection: add tests that reproduce past bugs from ENG-21047 and ENG-273654
rollout_notes: Soft launch: land library behind feature flag 'ts_streams_origami' in SDK canary builds for one week
Collect telemetry: instrument adapter to emit non-sensitive metrics (adapter_used, cancel_from_consumer, cancel_from_producer, partial_consumed_on_error) to help decide default behavior changes
Docs: update migration guide and include copy-paste snippet for common patterns (chat streaming UI, server-sent events bridge)
Deprecation: mark older examples that instruct manual conversion as legacy and link to new helper
Support: Solutions and DevRel will prepare a short notebook and a recording demonstrating common pitfalls and the recommended patterns
